title: La Liga investigates ‘die’ chants after Vinicius Junior scores in first game since alleged racist abuse
content:
Vinicius Junior scored, but Real Madrid lost 2-1 to Osasuna in their first game since the alleged racist abuse suffered by the Brazil forward in his side’s Champions League game against Benfica.

The 25-year-old forward turned home Madrid’s equaliser at Osasuna’s El Sadar Stadium in the 73rd minute after Ante Budimir’s 38th-minute opener from the penalty spot. The Brazil international celebrated by pointing to the name on the back of his shirt and making an “I’m here” gesture by pointing to the ground.

He was whistled by Osasuna fans during the game while there were chants of “Vinicius, balon de playa” — Vinicius, beach ball, a reference to how he missed out on the 2024 Ballon d’Or — and “tonto” (fool) against him. La Liga said after the game this it was also investigating footage that appeared to show Osasuna fans chanting “Vinicius, muerete”, which translates as “Vinicius, die”, during the game. The Athletic has contacted Osasuna for comment.

Vincius Jr has been previously targeted in this fixture and many others in Spain. In 2023, video footage was captured of an Osasuna supporter at El Sadar racially abusing Vinicius Jr during a game against Madrid. La Liga filed an official complaint to the Pamplona court (where Osasuna are based), but in 2024 the case was provisionally dismissed due to the “impossibility of identifying the perpetrator”.

UEFA is investigating the alleged racist abuse of Vinicius Jr by Benfica’s Argentine winger Gianluca Prestianni during Madrid’s Champions League play-off first leg at Lisbon’s Estadio da Luz on Tuesday.

Vinicius Jr opened the scoring in the 50th minute before celebrating in front of Benfica’s fans when he alerted referee Francois Letexier to something said. The match official subsequently activated FIFA’s protocol against alleged racist incidents by crossing his arms, and a 10-minute stoppage followed before play resumed. Both Benfica and Prestianni have vehemently denied the allegations.

Vinicius Jr’s goal against Osasuna was his first scored at an away ground in La Liga since September against Levante, but it was not enough to prevent a damaging defeat for Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. They are two points ahead of Barcelona at the top of La Liga, who could leapfrog their rivals back into first place with a win against Levante on Sunday.

“I hope it doesn’t mean anything, because we’re playing for our lives again in four days,” Arbeloa told his post-match press conference, when asked about the significance of the defeat.

“A team shows its strength in difficult times. There’s no room for doubts. I believe in my team. We need to maintain our high standards over time. We’ll keep working, pushing and getting the best out of every player, because we need them all.

“I’m not upset. Nobody likes to lose, least of all us. This is going to be a long season, I said it hadn’t started yet. And I still think the same, it was a first half where we had control, but we lacked speed. Against any low block, you have to move the ball faster.

“We need to be able to break down the flanks on both sides. We lean too much on the left wing, which is normal, but that makes us easy to defend against. We have another game on Wednesday (the second leg against Benfica at the Bernabeu) and we have to approach it in the best possible way.”

Budimir’s opener came after goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was judged to have fouled the Croatia striker, after he was initially shown a yellow card for simulation. Referee Alejandro Quintero gave the penalty after a VAR check and Budimir slotted past Courtois.

Vinicius Jr’s equaliser came after a run and pass from Federico Valverde, but the Uruguay international was then replaced by striker Gonzalo Garcia two minutes later. Osasuna substitute Raul Garcia gave his side the win late on, with Arbeloa asked afterwards about his decision to take off Valverde.

“He’s been putting in a lot of effort in many consecutive matches, despite being injured,” Arbeloa said. “He’s noticed it in recent weeks. And I preferred not to take any risks with Fede. It was more about not taking any risks, in case he got injured.”

Madrid are back in action on Wednesday in their play-off second leg against Jose Mourinho’s Benfica, the Portuguese coach’s first time back at the Bernabeu since his spell in charge there from 2010-2013 — and controversial comments suggesting Vinicius Jr had incited his alleged racist abuse with his celebration.

From The Athletic’s Real Madrid correspondent Guillermo Rai

Vinicius Jr always faces a hostile atmosphere when playing away, and Osasuna’s El Sadar Stadium was no different.

The Brazilian was greeted with boos from Osasuna fans as soon as he stepped off the team bus. He also had to deal with the usual chants of “Vinicius, balon de playa” and “tonto”. La Liga later said it was investigating footage that appeared to show Osasuna fans chanting ‘Vinicius, die’.

Amid it all Vinicius seemed calm and even put on a personal show during the warm-up, showing off his skills. He was once again Madrid’s biggest threat in attack, ahead of Kylian Mbappe — who is not 100 per cent fit due to discomfort in his left knee.

The 25-year-old faded after the break, but suddenly appeared to make it 1-1. It was the fourth game in a row in which Vinicius Jr has scored, raising his level under Arbeloa after the bad spell he went through under former coach Xabi Alonso.

On an individual level, the only blemish was a yellow card he was shown in the 88th minute, seemingly for protests to referee Quintero. He complained to Quintero about the fouls he received during the game and after both of Osasuna’s goals, which confirmed a damaging defeat for Arbeloa’s side.
